findings.title: Migration crashes when embed_category is unset or does not match a category
findings.body:
The query joins `site_settings` on `embed_category` and immediately indexes `[0]['id']`. If the `embed_category` setting was never saved (the default `''` is not stored) or its value matches no category name, the result is empty. `[0]` then returns nil and `nil['id']` raises NoMethodError, so the migration aborts on most sites.

Line 15 has the same flaw: `uncategorized_category_id` may also have no row in `site_settings`.

Fix: check the result size before indexing at both lines.

findings.title: Unescaped, unnormalized host values interpolated into SQL
findings.body:
Each line of the old `embeddable_hosts` setting is interpolated directly into the INSERT as `'#{h}'`. Problems:
- A value containing a quote breaks the statement and is an injection vector.
- Values are not stripped, so `\r`, surrounding whitespace and blank lines are inserted as-is.
- `http://` prefixes and paths are not removed.

The model's before_validation normalization is skipped here, so migrated rows such as `http://example.com` will never match `uri.host`. Previously working embeds would silently stop working.

Fix: quote values with `ActiveRecord::Base.connection.quote`, and strip/normalize each host (dropping blank lines) before inserting.

findings.title: before_validation raises on nil host
findings.body:
`self.host.sub!` is called unconditionally. If `host` is nil, e.g. the admin client omits it or `EmbeddableHost.new` is validated without a host, this raises NoMethodError and returns a 500 instead of a validation error.

Fix: guard with `if host.present?` or use safe navigation.

findings.title: Host lookup ignores ports and case inconsistently
findings.body:
The validation regex allows a port, and before_validation keeps it, e.g. `localhost.dev:3000` or `example.com:8080`. `record_for_host`, however, compares against `uri.host`, which never includes the port, so hosts saved with a port can never match.

Also, `lower(host)` is compared to `uri.host`, which is not downcased, so a referer with uppercase letters fails to match.

Fix: compare `lower(host) = ?` against `host.downcase`, and either strip ports on save or include `uri.port` in the comparison.

findings.title: update/destroy raise 500 on unknown id
findings.body:
`EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` returns nil for a missing record. `save_host(nil)` and `host.destroy` then raise NoMethodError, producing a 500 instead of a 404.

Fix: use `find` or raise `Discourse::NotFound`. `category_id` is also accepted without checking that the category exists.

findings.title: Plural `_ids` hydration assumes an array
findings.body:
Any key ending in `_ids` is now treated as an array of ids and `obj[k].map` is called on it. A null value or a non-array `_ids` attribute throws during hydration.

The `hydrated || []` fallback is dead code, since `map` always returns an array. Ids that are not found become `undefined` entries in the array.

Fix: guard with `Array.isArray(obj[k])` and filter out unresolved entries.

findings.title: `replace('_', '-')` only replaces the first underscore
findings.body:
`String.prototype.replace` with a string pattern replaces only the first occurrence. Any admin model type with more than one underscore would therefore not be found in `ADMIN_MODELS` and would be routed to `/` instead of `/admin/`.

Fix: use `type.replace(/_/g, '-')`.

findings.title: Test fetches fruit 2 but asserts fruit 1's data
findings.body:
The test calls `store.find('fruit', 2)` and asserts there are 2 colors with ids 1 and 2. Fruit 2 (banana) has only `color_ids: [3]`.

The test passes only because the pretender handler for `/fruits/:id` ignores the id and always returns `fruits[0]`. As written it is misleading and would fail if the mock were fixed.

Fix: query id 1, or make the mock respect `request.params.id`.

findings.title: Test name no longer matches behavior
findings.body:
`expandable_first_post?` no longer checks for embeddable hosts. The test "is false if embeddable_host is blank" now passes only because `embed_truncate` defaults to false, so it does not test what its name claims.

Fix: rename or remove the test.

findings.title: Fabricator file contents swapped
findings.body:
`category_fabricator.rb` now defines the `:embeddable_host` fabricator, while the new `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` contains all the category fabricators. It works because all fabricators are loaded, but it is confusing and looks like an accidental swap.

Fix: swap the contents back so each file holds its namesake fabricator.
